title: Bounded-above complexes with pseudo-coherent cohomology are pseudo-coherent
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and let $K\in D(R)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Suppose there exists an integer $b$ with $H^i(K)=0$ for every $i>b$, and for every integer $i$ the $R$-module $H^i(K)$, regarded as a complex concentrated in degree zero, is pseudo-coherent [def-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-complex]. Then $K$ is pseudo-coherent [def-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-complex].

proof.text: Choose a cochain complex $C^\bullet$ representing $K$ using [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Write $T_q=\tau_{\leq q}C^\bullet$, with terms $C^i$ for $i<q$, $\ker d_C^q$ for $i=q$, and zero for $i>q$, as in [lem-weil-pbc-truncation-triangle]. Directly from $H^i=\ker d^i/\operatorname{im}d^{i-1}$, the inclusion $T_q\to C^\bullet$ induces the identity on cohomology for $i<q$ and the identification $\ker d_C^q/\operatorname{im}d_C^{q-1}=H^q(C^\bullet)$ in degree $q$; above $q$ the cohomology of $T_q$ is zero. Thus $H^i(T_q)=H^i(K)$ for $i\leq q$ and $H^i(T_q)=0$ for $i>q$. If $q\geq b$, the inclusion is a quasi-isomorphism and hence gives $Q(T_q)\cong K$.

source.place: Section 0118, section-truncations, canonical truncations and their cohomology

proof.text: For each integer q, transport the pseudo-coherent degree-zero cohomology hypothesis to the module H^q(C) using the representative isomorphism Q(C) ≅ K and the cohomology factorization isomorphism. Shift its bounded-above finite-free representative by -q. The shifted complex is still bounded above, and its terms are finite free via the termwise shift isomorphisms. The commutation of Q with shifts and the single-functor shift isomorphism identify this model with the single complex H^q(C) placed in degree q. Thus that single complex is pseudo-coherent. Apply [lem-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-iff-all-m] to obtain m-pseudo-coherence for every m. This direct witness construction replaces iteration of the one-step m-pseudo-coherent shift lemma.

source.place: Tag 066B, lemma-cohomology-pseudo-coherent, shifted cohomology hypothesis; Tag 064U and the shift calculation in Tag 064R

proof.text: Put $B=\max(b,m-1)$. We prove that $Q(T_q)$ is $m$-pseudo-coherent for the finite sequence of integers $q=m-1,m,\ldots,B$. For the base $q=m-1$, Step 1 gives $H^i(T_{m-1})=0$ for every $i\geq m$. Apply [lem-pc-ring-m-pseudo-coherent-vanishing-base] with this same integer $m$. Equivalently, the zero bounded finite-free complex maps to $T_{m-1}$, inducing isomorphisms above $m$ and a surjection onto its zero degree-$m$ cohomology.

source.place: Tag 066B, lemma-cohomology-pseudo-coherent, induction base via Tag 064W (1)

proof.text: For the induction step let $m\leq q\leq B$ and assume $Q(T_{q-1})$ is $m$-pseudo-coherent. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-truncation-triangle] to $C^\bullet$ at $q$: it gives the distinguished triangle $Q(T_{q-1})\to Q(T_q)\to H^q(C^\bullet)[-q]\to Q(T_{q-1})[1]$. The first vertex is $m$-pseudo-coherent by induction, and the third is $m$-pseudo-coherent by Step 2 and $H^q(C^\bullet)\cong H^q(K)$. Apply the second clause of [lem-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-distinguished-triangle], with $A=Q(T_{q-1})$, $B=Q(T_q)$ and $C=H^q(C^\bullet)[-q]$, to conclude that the middle vertex is $m$-pseudo-coherent. This establishes the induction, including cohomology gaps, without requiring a largest nonzero degree.

source.place: Tag 066B, lemma-cohomology-pseudo-coherent, induction step via Tag 064R (2); truncation triangle from Derived Categories Tag 08J5

proof.text: At the endpoint $B\geq b$, Step 1 gives an isomorphism $Q(T_B)\cong K$. Compose the bounded finite-free approximation witnessing $m$-pseudo-coherence of $Q(T_B)$ with that isomorphism. Cohomology functors send the isomorphism to isomorphisms, so the composite is still an isomorphism on cohomology above $m$ and a surjection at $m$, precisely [def-pc-ring-m-pseudo-coherent]. Thus $K$ is $m$-pseudo-coherent. This argument also covers $b<m$, when $B=m-1$ and the induction has no steps.

source.place: Tag 066B, lemma-cohomology-pseudo-coherent, conclusion of the fixed-m induction

proof.text: Since $m$ was arbitrary, the representative $C^\bullet$ is $m$-pseudo-coherent for every integer $m$. Apply the converse of [lem-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-iff-all-m] to obtain a bounded-above finite-free representative of $K$, which is exactly pseudo-coherence. Each fixed-$m$ argument used only finitely many truncation triangles; no lower cohomology bound, Noetherian hypothesis or finite Tor-dimension hypothesis was used.

source.place: Tag 066B, lemma-cohomology-pseudo-coherent, final pseudo-coherent clause via Tag 064U
